name: cwk-ui
description: Point-and-click UI over the cwk-* Workflow Kit skills for non-technical roles (PM/SM). Runs Claude Code under the hood.

cwkUi.claudePath.description: Path to the Claude Code CLI executable. (machine-scoped: a workspace cannot override which binary is launched).

cwkUi.extraArgs.description: Extra args passed to `claude -p`. Default `--permission-mode acceptEdits`: skills may read and write inside the workspace (the KB, reports, code edits by the editing skills), and anything else a headless run would need a prompt for — arbitrary Bash (node for the map/PDF, npm/npx/jest, gh, curl), files outside the workspace, the network — is refused, so those steps surface as "error" here; use the Interactive button (a real terminal, where you answer the prompts) for them. Setting ["--permission-mode","bypassPermissions"] makes every step run headlessly, but it also permits ANY shell command, reading/writing files such as .env outside the workspace, and network calls with no prompt — and a prompt injection in a scanned repository can drive all of it. Anthropic recommends that mode only in an isolated environment; the panel warns once per session when it is set. The git-guard PreToolUse hook still blocks dangerous/remote git in every mode (hooks run before the permission check - verified), but it is defense-in-depth, not a sandbox. In readonly mode this setting cannot widen permissions: its permission flags are dropped and the CLI runs with `--permission-mode default` and a read-only tool allowlist.

cwkUi.usdToVnd.description: Approx VND per USD, shown next to the USD cost. Adjust to your rate; set 0 to hide VND.

cwkUi.model.description: DEFAULT model pre-selected in each form's Model dropdown (passed as `claude --model`). You can override it per run and per follow-up in the panel. 'sonnet' is ~5x cheaper than Opus for read-only Q&A/planning at great quality; 'haiku' is cheapest for simple lookups; 'opus' for the hardest code tasks; empty = your Claude default.

enumDescriptions: Every skill, including the seven that change code.

Only skills that never touch your source — for PM/SM. The code-editing cards are hidden, the host refuses them even if requested, and every run is launched with `--permission-mode default` and a read-only tool allowlist (Read, Grep, Glob, provenlens), so no prompt can run a shell command, write a file or reach the network.
cwkUi.mode.description: Which skills this panel offers, and what a run may do. 'readonly' hides the seven code-editing skills (build, fix-bug, migrate, simplify, perf, observe, rails-to-spring), blocks them plus free chat and follow-ups in the extension host, AND runs the CLI with `--permission-mode default --allowedTools Read,Grep,Glob,mcp__provenlens__*` — cwkUi.extraArgs cannot widen that. Use it for the .vsix you hand to non-developers.

enumDescriptions: Tiếng Việt — for a Vietnamese-speaking PM/SM.
cwkUi.language.description: Language for the panel's own labels and buttons. It does NOT change the language Claude answers in — that comes from the skill and from how you write the request.
